description:
Goal
Restore the accepted Elixir-shaped `call(args), do: body` item-macro surface that regressed when whitespace began distinguishing parenthesized calls from no-parens calls. This blocks the def/defp corpus migration because `fz2 test` readiness fixtures use this form.

Signal
An adjacent frontdoor test proves `test(:passes), do: assert(true)` parses as one `test/2` AST call with a fresh `[do: ...]` argument, and both `fz2 test` readiness/timeout integration tests pass through JIT and interpreter paths.

Strategy
Make the general call grammar own comma-keyword trailing bodies for parenthesized calls. Reuse the existing trailing-do attachment authority; do not special-case `test`, `def`, or item position. Preserve the existing rule that `echo(label: :work) do ... end` keeps its two keyword lists distinct.

Removal/collapse
Collapse comma-do and do/end attachment into the same call-body path if possible. Do not add a compatibility recognizer or reconstructed AST.

Acceptance
Focused parser and integration tests pass, the full library suite is green, documentation/comments describe the shared grammar accurately, and a fresh holistic review has no findings.
title: Preserve comma-do attachment after parenthesized macro calls
